title: Closed predicates and equality are detected on a dense subset
statement: Let $X$ be a metric space and $D\subseteq X$ a dense subset, meaning every open neighbourhood [def-kun-open-neighbourhood] of every point of $X$ meets $D$. If a predicate $P$ on $X$ has closed truth set $\{x\in X:P(x)\}$ and holds at every point of $D$, then $P$ holds on all of $X$. In particular, if $Y$ is a metric space and $u,v:X\to Y$ are continuous maps with $u(a)=v(a)$ for every $a\in D$, then $u=v$. A subset is closed when its complement is open.
